# How to succeed in this course {#how-to-succeed}

Success in QM is not about talent for mathematics. It is about running a
short, repeatable weekly cycle: **prepare before class, work actively in
class, practise after class, and bring your attempts to the tutorial.** Every
lecture chapter is built around this cycle, and every part of it carries a
stated time budget so you always know what "enough" looks like.

Why this rhythm works: preparation means the lecture is your *second* pass
over each idea, not your first, so class time can go into worked examples and
questions instead of definitions. Same-day retrieval interrupts forgetting
when it is cheapest to fix. Spaced review items in each chapter keep earlier
lectures warm, because the exam is cumulative. And the tutorials only work as
exam preparation if you arrive with attempts --- including wrong ones, which
are the most useful kind.

The total ask outside class: about **3.5 hours per week** for QM Basic in
two-lecture weeks (less in tutorial weeks), and about **2 hours per week**
for QM Intermediate. That is the whole plan. Students who spread these hours
as scheduled below consistently outperform students who batch them before
the exam.

## The calendar at a glance

Both courses run in weeks 43--49 of Block 2.

**QM Basic (year 1):** Monday 14:45 and Thursday 10:45 sessions, in a fixed
cadence of three lectures then a tutorial, four times.

| Week | Monday | Thursday |
|---|---|---|
| 43 | Lecture 1 | Lecture 2 |
| 44 | Lecture 3 | Tutorial 1 |
| 45 | Lecture 4 | Lecture 5 |
| 46 | Lecture 6 | Tutorial 2 |
| 47 | Lecture 7 | Lecture 8 |
| 48 | Lecture 9 | Tutorial 3 |
| 49 | Lecture 10 | Tutorial 4 |

**QM Intermediate (year 2):** one lecture per week on Wednesday, but the
time varies by week (08:45, 10:45, 12:45, or 14:45) --- always confirm the

week's lecture.

| Week | Lecture (Wed) | Tutorial |
|---|---|---|
| 43 | Lecture 1 | --- |
| 44 | Lecture 2 | --- |
| 45 | Lecture 3 | Tutorial 1 (Thu) |
| 46 | Lecture 4 | --- |
| 47 | Lecture 5 | --- |

## Printable weekly checklists

Four week types cover the whole block. Print this page (the checklists print
cleanly without the site navigation) or copy the relevant list into your
planner at the start of each week.

### QM Basic --- week with two lectures (weeks 43, 45, 47)

::: {.week-checklist}
#### Two-lecture week --- about 3.5 hours outside class

- <span class="day">Friday before</span> (30 min, free morning): prep videos
  for Monday's lecture, prep task, prediction
- <span class="day">Monday</span>: 14:45 lecture · evening, 15 min retrieval
- <span class="day">Tuesday</span> (60 min, free day): practice for Monday's
  lecture (worked, faded, unassisted) · flagged review items from earlier
  lectures
- <span class="day">Wednesday</span> (45 min, around the single EiA slot):
  prep videos for Thursday's lecture, prep task, prediction
- <span class="day">Thursday</span>: 10:45 lecture · afternoon, 15 min
  retrieval
- <span class="day">Friday</span> (60 min): practice for Thursday's lecture ·
  utility prompt, two sentences · start next week's loop (prep for Monday)
:::

### QM Basic --- week with one lecture and a tutorial (weeks 44, 46, 48, 49)

::: {.week-checklist}
#### Lecture-plus-tutorial week

- <span class="day">Friday before</span> (30 min): prep for Monday's lecture
- <span class="day">Monday</span>: 14:45 lecture · 15 min retrieval
- <span class="day">Tuesday</span> (60 min): practice for Monday's lecture
- <span class="day">Wednesday</span> (60 min): attempt the tutorial tasks
  yourself first, AI allowed under the protocol, mark stuck points
- <span class="day">Thursday</span>: 10:45 tutorial (exam prep session),
  bring attempts · 15 min: redo the missed task
- <span class="day">Friday</span> (60 min): finish the tutorial set
  unassisted · utility prompt · prep for Monday
:::

### QM Intermediate --- standard week (one Wednesday lecture)

The year 2 week is denser (two or three other lectures plus EiA3 and their
tutorials), so the QM cycle is one loop, spread wide.

::: {.week-checklist}
#### Standard week --- about 2 hours outside class

- <span class="day">Monday or Tuesday</span> (30 min, before the lecture):
  prep video, prep question, R warm-up, bring the output
- <span class="day">Wednesday</span>: QM lecture (check the time, it changes
  by week) · evening, 15 min retrieval
- <span class="day">Thursday or Friday</span> (60--75 min, around your EiA3
  slot): after-class practice --- faded task, unassisted set, the
  full-pipeline item where the set has one · one review item from an earlier
  lecture · utility prompt, two sentences about your EiA3 venture
:::

### QM Intermediate --- tutorial week (weeks 45 and 48)

The tutorial is the day after the lecture, so attempts cannot wait for the
end of the week. The tutorial covers the three preceding lectures, and only
its last part depends on Wednesday's lecture --- the task sheets are ordered
to match, and that ordering is deliberate.

::: {.week-checklist}
#### Tutorial week

- <span class="day">Monday or Tuesday</span> (75 min): prep for Wednesday's
  lecture (30) · attempt the tutorial tasks that rest on the earlier
  lectures (45), AI allowed under the protocol, mark stuck points
- <span class="day">Wednesday</span>: QM lecture · evening, 30 min: attempt
  the remaining tutorial tasks that use today's material
- <span class="day">Thursday</span>: tutorial (exam prep session), bring
  attempts and stuck points
- <span class="day">Friday</span> (45 min): redo what the tutorial
  corrected, unassisted · utility prompt
:::

## Working with AI, in one paragraph

Use [Tilly](https://chatbot.tilburg.ai/) and other AI tools under the
standing protocol **Attempt → Ask → Verify → Explain**: attempt the task
yourself first and locate exactly where you are stuck; ask for a hint or a
diagnostic question rather than a full solution; verify everything against
the data, the course notation, and R output; then explain the result in your
own words. The exam tests what *you* can do with supplied output; the
protocol makes AI sharpen that ability instead of replacing it.

## If you fall behind

Do not try to catch up by reading. Go to the most recent lecture's chapter,
do its retrieval set, then its faded task, and bring what breaks to the next
tutorial or to Tilly. One completed cycle on the current lecture is worth
more than three passive re-reads of older ones. The
[Mathematics Refresher](math-refresher.qmd) and
[R Refresher](r-refresher.qmd) exist precisely so that a gap from an earlier
course never blocks this one.
